articles.title: Kenneth Walker III ruled out vs. Bills on Thanksgiving due to groin issue
articles.summary: Kenneth Walker III was in the midst of his finest season in the NFL prior to the injury.
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs will not have star running back Kenneth Walker III for another game. Despite returning to practice Tuesday, Walker was ruled out for their game against the Buffalo Bills on Thanksgiving, the team announced. .

It will mark the third straight game Walker will miss due to the issue.

Prior to the injury, Walker was well on his way toward posting his finest season in the NFL. Through eight games, the running back already rushed for 872 yards and seven touchdowns. He also hauled in 26 catches for 172 yards and four receiving scores.

But Walker reported groin soreness just days ahead of the team's Week 10 game against the Atlanta Falcons. The Chiefs decided to hold Walker out for the contest , initially implying it would be a short-term issue.

Walker, however, was unable to return to practice ahead of Week 11, and also missed that game . The Chiefs won in both Week 10 and Week 11 without Walker.

After missing Monday's practice, Walker was able to return to the field Tuesday. He was listed as a limited participant during that practice.

Despite that, the Chiefs apparently determined Walker was not ready to return from his injury just yet.

Following the team's Thanksgiving game in Week 12, the Chiefs will play once again on Thursday in Week 13, when they will take on the Los Angeles Rams.

articles.title: Josh Allen turns down an unusual request from Kansas City Chiefs coach, leaving rivalry tensions in focus
articles.summary: Josh Allen has no plans to retire, despite Kansas City Chiefs defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo’s wish.
articles.body: Josh Allen has no plans to retire, despite Kansas City Chiefs defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo’s wish. The coach made the unusual request after Buffalo’s 28-21 win over Kansas City last season, a result that snapped the Chiefs’ winning run and helped derail their season. With the teams meeting on Thanksgiving night, Spagnuolo revisited the exchange this week. Allen smiled at the memory, but his answer was clear: he is not ready to leave, and this rivalry has more chapters. The timing adds another layer, with both sides preparing for a high-stakes divisional meeting.Josh Allen keeps Spagnuolo’s retirement request on holdAs the Democrat & Chronicle reported, Spagnuolo said his request still stands. After last year’s loss, he approached Allen and told him, “I don’t want to play you anymore. I want you to retire.”Spagnuolo explained why Allen remains such a difficult matchup for Kansas City.“I wish he had. He didn’t listen to me, though. He didn’t listen to me,” Spagnuolo said. “It just seems like when he plays the Kansas City Chiefs, he’s on fire. He becomes Superman. Somehow, we’ve got to force him into a bad throw, or somebody comes up with a really big play.”Allen laughed when reminded of the request. He said he might take Spagnuolo up on it one day, but not soon.“Not retired yet,” Allen said. “Hopefully we have a long time before then, but I’ve got so much respect for him and his defense. The different looks that they can present and kind of show you one thing and bringing the complete opposite. They’re extremely well coached and it’s always a tough test against these guys.”The joke reflects a serious challenge: Kansas City still needs a way to limit Allen.Spagnuolo sees a quarterback in controlSpagnuolo called Allen a “cerebral” quarterback and praised his connection with Bills head coach Joe Brady. Their familiarity, he said, gives Buffalo a clear plan.“I think he’s been with Joe Brady, now this is either the third or fourth year, and they’re in lockstep and sync,” Spagnuolo said. “They know exactly what they want to do and I would expect that same thing to happen in this game. So, the challenge with Josh is not only his physical challenge, but it’s his mental challenge. He’s a veteran now, but he’s one of those guys that has complete control at the line of scrimmage, and he gets the last say. And I think Josh is really good at it.”Allen’s recent production has been less imposing. Over his last five games, he has 1,023 passing yards, five touchdowns and five interceptions. He has three rushing scores in that stretch, but averages just 10 rushing yards per game.Against Miami last week, Allen did not attempt a rush despite playing more than one snap. It was the first such game of his career.Rain and wind are forecast for Thursday, potentially making throws harder to complete. Buffalo could lean more on Allen’s legs and running back James Cook. Spagnuolo’s retirement request may have to wait; stopping Allen is the more immediate task.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: NHL Injury Update: Why has Alex Ovechkin's viral pregame video raised fresh questions about his physical condition with the Washington Capitals
articles.summary: A viral pregame video featuring Alex Ovechkin raises questions about the Capitals captain's physical condition as he faces a scoring slump in his farewell NHL season.
articles.body: A casual pregame video of veteran forward Alex Ovechkin and Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels circulating online has become a talking point among Washington Capitals fans about the physical condition of the Russian star. The video, posted on ESPN by the NFL, showed the two Washington sports stars throwing a football back and forth, but the exchange drew some surprising reactions from hockey fans.The conversation comes at a difficult time for Ovechkin’s farewell NHL season. The 41-year-old forward has fallen into an uncharacteristic scoring slump, and his reduced ice time and lack of production have some wondering about his current form and whether he can finish his final campaign with a flourish.Why Alex Ovechkin's viral video has Washington Capitals fans concernedThe video, which went viral, has sparked a debate about the physical condition of Alex Ovechkin, especially as it appeared at one of the most difficult moments of his recent NHL career. But the video doesn’t show that the Washington Capitals captain is injured or unable to play physically.This week, NFL on ESPN shared the footage of the meeting between two prominent Washington sports personalities. Ovechkin was standing next to Jayden Daniels, and it was a cute moment that quickly became a story outside of just football.What do Alex Ovechkin's NHL statistics reveal?The numbers provide a clearer explanation for the growing concern surrounding the Washington Capitals captain.Ovechkin went 16 consecutive games without scoring through Saturday, a career-first drought across his previous 1,578 NHL appearances. He had recorded just one goal in 21 games this season, converting only 2.7% of his 37 shots.The drop in playing time is particularly apparent as Ovechkin already registered a career-low average of 17:26 last season. His current average is another significant drop in his role.Why does this scoring slump matter for Alex Ovechkin's farewell season?Ovechkin confirmed in early October that the 2026-27 campaign would be his final NHL season. That announcement added significance to every milestone and performance as the veteran prepares to leave professional hockey.What comes next for the Washington Capitals captain?Ovechkin has the Capitals’ remaining schedule to pick up some momentum. After the Philadelphia Flyers game on Wednesday, November 25, the team will play the Florida Panthers on Friday, November 27.The next game could be another opportunity for the veteran forward to snap out of his scoring slump and get some confidence back for the rest of the season.But Ovechkin’s career accomplishments are still remarkable, controversy over the viral video aside. articles.title: Eagles roster news: 3 moves announced ahead of Cowboys game
articles.summary: Week 12 updates.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles officially announced three roster moves ahead of their Week 12 Thanksgiving game against the Dallas Cowboys.

DT Gabe Hall was signed from the practice squad to the active roster.

EDGE Mason Reiger and S Cole Wisniewski were temporarily elevated from the practice squad to the roster.

Note: teams are permitted to temporarily elevate up to two practice squad players per game . A player can be elevated up to three times in the regular season and an unlimited number of times in the postseason.

Let's sort through this news on a player-by-player basis.

The Eagles previously temporarily elevated Hall for their Week 11 game against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Despite playing just eight snaps on defense, Hall logged one sack (potentially making him the last player to ever sack Aaron Rodgers) and one tackle for loss.

One can wonder if Hall's performance caught attention from other teams, prompting the Eagles to put him on their roster so that he couldn't be poached from the practice squad.

The Eagles now have five defensive tackles on their roster: Jalen Carter, Moro Ojomo, Byron Young, Ty Robinson, and Hall. They also still have Leki Fotu and Zion Wilson on the practice squad.

With Arnold Ebiketie ruled out, the Eagles elevated Reiger to have more edge rusher depth. Reiger will likely only play on special teams, just like he did the last time the team temporarily elevated him. He has one remaining elevation this season, as does fellow rookie edge defender Keyshawn James-Newby.

This marks Wisniewski's third and final elevation for the 2026 season. He's set to contribute on special teams in addition to providing depth at safety.

articles.title: Steelers officially announced they have waived Aaron Rodgers
articles.summary: In a whirlwind 24 hours, the Steelers benched, deactivated and then finally released quarterback Aaron Rodgers.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers rollercoaster started around 10 PM Eastern on Tuesday night with the news that the Steelers were benching and planned to deactivate quarterback Aaron Rodgers for Friday's game against the Denver Broncos . This took everyone by surprise but when it happened we had no idea that less than 24 hours later, the drama would culminate with the Steelers releasing Rodgers.

We may never know exactly what the events were that led up to all this behind the scenes but we do know that within 30 minutes of Rodgers going on the Pat McAfee Show and throwing head coach Mike McCarthy under the bus for 20 minutes, the reports of Pittsburgh planning to release Rodgers were already out there. McAfee himself reported it later in the same show and was flabbergasted how quickly everything happened.

Since the release came after the NFL trade deadline, Rodgers went on waivers. Teams can claim Rodgers until 4 p.m. ET today, Thursday, November 26, 2026.

articles.title: Micah Parsons Reacts to Packers' Loss vs. Rams and Struggles Stopping Blake Corum, Kyren Williams
articles.summary: Wednesday's 26-13 loss to the Los Angeles Rams was a game to forget for the Green Bay Packers, but there was at least one silver lining.
articles.body:
Wednesday's 26-13 loss to the Los Angeles Rams was a game to forget for the Green Bay Packers, but there was at least one silver lining.

Micah Parsons played his first game since December as he returned from a torn ACL that cut short his 2025 campaign and delayed the start of his 2026 season. Not only did he return, he sacked Matthew Stafford in the second quarter when the Packers were building momentum.

It was a welcome sight for a Green Bay defense that has largely missed his production as one of the best pass-rushers in the league, but it did little to make him feel better about the Packers' overall performance.

Speaking to reporters after the game, Parsons lamented the fact that the Green Bay defense allowed the Rams to rush for 241 yards as a team, including 184 yards and a touchdown from Blake Corum, and 46 yards and a touchdown from Kyren Williams.

"We need to figure out who's going to be a dog or not," Parsons said. "Like that's just the reality of it. To me, to be honest, and this is around the league, if someone can line up 50 times and run down your mouth and you don't have an answer for it, that is player ... that's accountability. That's just how I really feel about it."

Per ESPN's Rob Demovsky , Parsons played only 37 percent of the Packers' defensive snaps in his first action of the season, and that was largely due to the Rams' ground game keeping them out of obvious passing situations.

Parsons commented on the Rams managing to largely neutralize with their run game, saying, "I wasn't able to get on the field because of it, because they didn't want to waste my plays on first and second down. I think the whole thing is just bad, and we've got to figure out who's willing to play with us or who's playing against us at this point because every quarter, every minute, every down matters and we've got to figure out who's in this for the long haul and who's in it for the ride."

While Parsons provided reason for optimism with the sack, the Green Bay defense gradually wore down as the game progressed.

A Rams team that was playing without Puka Nacua and Davante Adams continued to rely on Corum and the rushing attack to much success.

Stafford didn't have to do much, as the home team controlled the second half and the clock with that ground attack.

On the other side, Green Bay's offense wasn't the same in the second half after wide receiver Christian Watson was sidelined with a concussion . Watson scored in the first half, but the Rams could focus more attention on Matthew Golden with his running mate ruled out.

As a result, Jordan Love threw two interceptions and the offense completely stalled while failing to score a point in the second half.

There wasn't much to feel good about for the Packers in the loss, but at least Parsons looked like his normal self while tallying a sack.

Green Bay now finds itself in a difficult spot with six games left to play, though, as the Packers' 6-5 record places them one game behind the Los Angeles Rams for the final wild-card spot in the NFC.

articles.title: Everything Stafford, McVay Said About Rams' Win vs. Packers in 1st-Ever NFL Thanksgiving Eve Game
articles.summary: Having won five straight games after a 26-13 victory over the Green Bay Packers in the NFL's first Thanksgiving Eve game on Wednesday night, the Los Angeles Rams are starting to look like the juggernaut they were expected to be at the start of the season.
articles.body:
Having won five straight games after a 26-13 victory over the Green Bay Packers in the NFL's first Thanksgiving Eve game on Wednesday night, the Los Angeles Rams are starting to look like the juggernaut they were expected to be at the start of the season.

Rams head coach Sean McVay was particularly effusive in his praise of how this group has rallied despite having a depleted group of pass-catchers with Puka Nacua, Davante Adams and Terrance Ferguson out with injuries (starts at 3:40 mark).

"What you learn is, every single week you've got to adjust and adapt," McVay said. "The game honors toughness, and I think we're playing tougher. We're learning how to establish possession."

Matthew Stafford echoed his coach's sentiments about their ability to adapt, particularly this game on a drive-to-drive basis, and praised how well the defense has been playing to elevate the team with the offense needing to manufacture yards in different ways (starts at 8:25 mark):

"Obviously, a lot of adjustments needed to be made, kind of within the drives and within the game on offense. Guys that stepped in did a hell of a job. Had a couple guys kind of go out, come back in. But just proud of the effort, proud of our team. Defense played fantastic again, and we were able to control the line of scrimmage, which was the recipe for success today."

The Rams have turned to a run-heavy approach with their top two receivers and No. 1 tight end unavailable, with the results being extremely positive.

Los Angeles racked up 241 yards on the ground against the Packers after running for 202 in its previous game against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 10.

It's the first time the Rams have run for at least 200 yards in consecutive games since the 1984 season.

Blake Corum has become the go-to guy in the offense. He set career-highs in carries (32), rushing yards (184) and scrimmage yards (205) against the Packers.

The 32 rushing attempts were nearly double Corum's previous career-high of 17 set earlier this season in two different games.

One key of being able to run the ball is the Rams are taking a lot of pressure off Stafford. He has only attempted 49 passes in the last two games after throwing the ball 43 times in Week 9 against the Washington Commanders.

The Rams (7-4) have put themselves back in the mix for a playoff spot in the NFC. They are currently in the final wild-card spot with six games remaining in the regular season.

Things won't get easier for the Rams as they look to keep their winning streak going with their next two games against the Kansas City Chiefs and San Francisco 49ers.

articles.title: New Aaron Rodgers Rumors on 'Ultimatum' Given to Steelers' McCarthy, 'Run Things My Way, or I Quit'
articles.summary: Before the Pittsburgh Steelers decided to bench and ultimately release quarterback Aaron Rodgers this week, Rodgers reportedly approached head coach Mike McCarthy with an "ultimatum" regarding the offense.
articles.body:
Before the Pittsburgh Steelers decided to bench and ultimately release quarterback Aaron Rodgers this week, Rodgers reportedly approached head coach Mike McCarthy with an "ultimatum" regarding the offense.

According to Tom Pelissero of Netflix Sports, Rodgers wanted changes to be made to the offensive play-calling process, and effectively told McCarthy, "Run things my way, or I quit."

Shortly thereafter, the Steelers announced on Tuesday night that Mason Rudolph would be the team's starting quarterback Friday against the Denver Broncos, and that Rodgers would be inactive.

Then, after Rodgers was highly critical of McCarthy during an appearance on the Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday, the Steelers released the future Hall of Fame quarterback.

On the Pat McAfee Show , Rodgers alleged that McCarthy has been late to meetings and even fallen asleep during them this season.

Per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo (h/t ESPN ), Rodgers recently approached McCarthy about taking over the offensive play-calling duties himself. When McCarthy balked at the idea, they discussed the compromise of quarterbacks coach Tom Arth being the one who relay the plays to Rodgers.

Pelissero said Wednesday night that "frustration had been building" among some coaches and teammates with Rodgers over his penchant for calling plays himself and getting away from the running game that had been so effective earlier in the season.

While McCarthy was reportedly "open" to making some changes to the play-calling process in order to accommodate Rodgers, McCarthy received feedback from coaches and some players that they didn't want that to happen, per Pelissero.

After a 6-2 start to the season, the Steelers have lost back-to-back games, and the offense struggled mightily in both of those defeats.

Pittsburgh managed just 222 yards of offense in a 38-18 loss to the Cincinnati Bengals, and 255 total yards in a 19-16 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.

The Steelers still hold an AFC wild-card playoff spot currently with a 6-4 mark, but if they are going to reach the postseason, they will now have to do it without Rodgers.

Pelissero noted that the Steelers organization is backing McCarthy despite the accusations made by Rodgers on Wednesday, and he is being entrusted to make a playoff push with Rudolph as his quarterback.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers 'Frustrated' Steelers Players & Coaches by 'Calling Plays Himself,' New Rumors Reveal
articles.summary: One day after Aaron Rodgers went scorched earth on Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy over his frustrations with how things have played out this season, it turns out there was unhappiness in the locker room with some things the veteran quarterback was doing on the field.
articles.body:
One day after Aaron Rodgers went scorched earth on Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy over his frustrations with how things have played out this season, it turns out there was unhappiness in the locker room with some things the veteran quarterback was doing on the field.

On Netflix's pregame show prior to the Thanksgiving Eve game, The Ringer's Tom Pelissero reported Steelers coaches and some players had grown "frustrated" with Rodgers "calling plays himself" during games in recent weeks.

One of the things Rodgers spoke about during his explosive appearance on The Pat McAfee Show was wanting a heavier input on the offense and calling plays himself.

According to Rodgers, there was a discussion with McCarthy about quarterbacks coach Tom Arth handling play-calling duties and McCarthy seemed onboard before changing his mind.

NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reported earlier on Wednesday that the Steelers were in the process of changing their play-calling structure with Arth set to take over at Rodgers' request.

At some point in the process, the Steelers had a change of heart and announced late Tuesday that Rodgers was being benched with Mason Rudolph set to take over as the starter against the Denver Broncos on Black Friday.

The situation led to Rodgers' appearance on Pat McAfee's show in which he seemingly unleashed everything he could ever want to say about McCarthy, prompting the Steelers to announce they released him.

Rodgers was in his second season with the Steelers. It was the first year of the Rodgers-McCarthy pairing after McCarthy was hired as head coach in January to replace Mike Tomlin.

The Steelers got off to a strong 6-2 start, but they have lost back-to-back games since their Week 9 bye. The offense has scored a total of 34 points in those two losses and has been held under 20 points in three of the last four games.

articles.title: Jordan Love Takes Blame After 2 INT in Packers' Loss vs. Rams in 1st-Ever Thanksgiving Eve Game
articles.summary: Quarterback Jordan Love placed the blame on himself following the Green Bay Packers' 26-13 loss to the Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday night.
articles.body:
Quarterback Jordan Love placed the blame on himself following the Green Bay Packers' 26-13 loss to the Los Angeles Rams on Wednesday night.

Speaking to reporters after the game, Love said, "Not good enough. Definitely not. We'll see when we look at it, but just not good, especially second half. I know where my play needs to be and obviously it starts with me, so I've got to be a lot better."

Love completed 17 of his 29 passing attempts for 198 yards with one touchdown and two interceptions. Both of those interceptions occurred in the second half, as Green Bay was shut out over the game's final 30 minutes.

Green Bay was highly competitive during the first half, entering the break tied 13-13 with the Rams in a tightly contested road game.

However, things appeared to change significantly for the Packers' offense when wide receiver Christian Watson left the game late in the first half after getting concussed on a hit by Rams safety Kam Kinchens.

Watson, who scored the Packers' only touchdown of the night, has enjoyed a breakout 2026 season, setting career highs in receptions (56), receiving yards (981) and touchdowns (eight).

Second-year wideout Matthew Golden has also been a revelation for Green Bay with 59 catches for 892 yards and five touchdowns, but with Watson not on the field to command some of the defensive attention, L.A. held Golden without a catch in the second half.

On top of the Packers' offense sputtering after halftime, the Green Bay defense had no answers for the Rams' running game.

Los Angeles rushed for 241 yards as a team, led by a career-high 184 yards on the ground by running back Blake Corum.

The loss marked Green Bay's second in a row, dropping it to 6-5 on the season, which would not be good enough for a playoff spot if the regular season ended today.

While the Packers still have six games left to right the ship and get back to the playoffs for a fourth consecutive season, there are some glaring holes that need to be addressed.

The run defense's struggles prevented the Green Bay offense from seeing the field much in the second half, and the run offense's issues allowed the L.A. defense to key on stopping Love and the passing game.

Green Bay rushed for just 55 yards on Wednesday and ranks last in the NFL with 65.9 rushing yards per game.

The running game could potentially receive a boost as soon as next week, though, if running back Josh Jacobs is able to return from a finger injury that has kept him out since Week 9.

articles.title: Mike McCarthy's ice cream sandwich assistant idea gets rave reviews from Kevin Durant on Thanksgiving
articles.summary: Kevin Durant views Mike McCarthy as an innovator.
articles.body:
It's a real shame the sports world learned about Mike McCarthy's ice cream sandwich assistant after Halloween. Given the absurdity of that revelation , the Pittsburgh Steelers coach's ice cream pal would have been a popular costume among sports fans looking to have fun with the moment.

Thankfully, McCarthy's ice cream sandwich assistant is also perfectly in theme for the next big holiday. Thanksgiving is here in the United States, and, as you might have guessed, McCarthy's assistant is getting a little extra attention as fans and sports stars get ready to sit down for a day of gluttonous behavior.

Houston Rockets star Kevin Durant was among the biggest names to reference McCarthy's ice cream sandwich assistant on Thanksgiving. Durant called the move a "great idea," and said he would be hiring an ice cream assistant of his own on the holiday.

If you somehow missed the whole McCarthy saga, well, here's a refresher. After learning he was being benched by the Steelers, quarterback Aaron Rodgers went on Pat McAfee's show and completely blasted his own head coach.

Rodgers said, frankly, a lot of wild things. He claimed McCarthy fell asleep in team meetings regularly and broke down the Steelers with a chant of "1-2-3 Packers" during their last game. Some of those claims have been confirmed by local media or McCarthy himself.

But the ice cream sandwich assistant has even shadier origins. As all the Rodgers madness was popping off, former Steelers defensive tackle Breiden Fehoko claimed McCarthy had an ice cream sandwich assistant, someone responsible for bringing the coach an ice cream sandwich on demand. Fehoko claimed he received that information from a Steelers player.

That report has not been confirmed by local reporters or McCarthy himself, though that's not going to stop sports fans from having a little fun. McCarthy's ice cream sandwich assistant received a fair amount of attention Wednesday. And if Durant's tweet is any indication, the rumor is going to remain in the spotlight Thursday.

It makes sense. After polishing off multiple plates of food, who isn't willing to pay a relative to bring dessert directly to them as they try and see if their previously stuffed stomach can handle a little sweet treat without exploding?

articles.title: Steelers Players Watched Aaron Rodgers on Pat McAfee's Show from the Bathroom, Reveals NFL Insider
articles.summary: As Aaron Rodgers was unloading on Mike McCarthy during an appearance on The Pat McAfee Show, his Pittsburgh Steelers teammates were watching the situation unfold in a unique part of the team's facilities.
articles.body:
As Aaron Rodgers was unloading on Mike McCarthy during an appearance on The Pat McAfee Show , his Pittsburgh Steelers teammates were watching the situation unfold in a unique part of the team's facilities.

Per The Athletic's Mike DeFabo , many Steelers players were "huddled in the bathroom" to watch Rodgers' final words as a member of the organization.

The Steelers' practice began at 12 p.m. local time and was scheduled to run for two hours, but DeFabo noted they cut it short to end at 1:40 p.m. It just so happens that was when Rodgers showed up on McAfee's show.

Russell Wilson Reacts to Aaron Rodgers Calling Out Steelers' Mike McCarthy in McAfee Video

Media members did get access to the Steelers' locker room soon after practice ended. Rookie quarterback Drew Allar was the only one who spoke during that period before veteran safety DeShon Elliott stepped in to cut things off knowing what was going on with Rodgers.

According to DeFabo, some players did poke their heads into the locker room and "darted out" upon seeing reporters.

Rodgers' appearance with McAfee came in the wake of the Steelers announcing late Tuesday night they were going to start Mason Rudolph for the Black Friday game against the Denver Broncos and the four-time NFL MVP would be inactive.

In the wake of Rodgers' comments about McCarthy, the Steelers released him in what could be the final act of his Hall-of-Fame career. He finished his Pittsburgh tenure with 2,241 passing yards and 16 touchdowns in 10 games this season.

articles.title: Week 12 Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Advice on Fantasy Football Stars to Play or Bench
articles.summary: Week 12 got underway on Wednesday night, and the action will pick back up with the Detroit Lions and Chicago Bears at 1 p.m. ET on Thursday. Fantasy managers who haven't set their lineups yet need to do so, and they must pay attention to the rest of the week's schedule.
articles.body:
Week 12 got underway on Wednesday night, and the action will pick back up with the Detroit Lions and Chicago Bears at 1 p.m. ET on Thursday. Fantasy managers who haven't set their lineups yet need to do so, and they must pay attention to the rest of the week's schedule.

The Week 12 slate includes three games on Thursday and one on Friday, in addition to the normal Sunday and Monday games.

While all 32 teams are in action this week, injuries and bad matchups may still leave many managers leaning on second-tier options. Here, you'll find the top remaining plays for Week 12 and some start/sit advice for point-per-reception (PPR) scoring.

Kirk Cousins struggled against the San Francisco 49ers in Mexico City last Sunday, as did the rest of the Minnesota Vikings. However, he flashed his fantasy potential the previous week, delivering a solid 16.4 points in his 2026 Vikings debut.

Cousins is a viable streamer this week, as the Vikings will host a very inconsistent Atlanta Falcons team. Atlanta has surrendered the eighth-most fantasy points to opposing QBs this season.

Sit: Baker Mayfield, Tampa Bay Buccaneers

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers just can't seem to get their passing attack off the ground. Baker Mayfield's series of injuries certainly hasn't helped, but a lack of reliable targets and some questionable scheming by coordinator Zac Robinson have been the biggest issues.

Those issues may be alleviated somewhat against a faltering Carolina Panthers secondary. However, Tampa is quite likely to attack the Panthers with the ground game early and often. Mayfield may simply not have the volume needed to come through for fantasy managers.

Christian McCaffrey, San Francisco 49ers

Start: Kenny Gainwell, Tampa Bay Buccaneers

Bucky Irving is an obvious must-start against a Panthers defense that has surrendered the second-most fantasy points to opposing RBs. However, backup Kenny Gainwell is also worth a start in Week 12.

Gainwell and Irving were both stymied by a good Detroit Lions run defense last week. Gainwell still caught four passes and reached 9.9 fantasy points, though, and he reached double digits in each of his previous two games.

Like Gainwell, Seattle Seahawks back Zach Charbonnet finds himself in a backfield committee. However, he doesn't have as much upside behind Jadarian Price, and he has yet to reach double-digit fantasy points in any of his three games since returning from last year's ACL tear.

This week, the Seahawks will visit the San Francisco 49ers, who have surrendered the seventh-fewest fantasy points to opposing running backs this season. Other Week 12 RB sits:

There's a non-zero chance that the Lions and Chicago Bears engage in an aerial track meet on Thursday. Both teams have been good against the run recently and middling against the pass—Detroit and Chicago have each surrendered north of 25 fantasy points per week to opposing receivers.

This should create a big opportunity for Detroit's No. 2 wideout, Jameson Williams, who came through with a whopping 19.3 fantasy points last week.

Deebo Samuel was a big piece of the 49ers' passing attack earlier in the season, specifically, while Mike Evans was sidelined. With Evans back in the lineup and Keenan Allen also on the roster, it's difficult to trust Samuel moving forward.

Samuel had just 7.7 fantasy points last week and could struggle again versus Seattle. No team has surrendered fewer fantasy points to opposing wide receivers this season than the Seahawks.

Start: T.J. Hockenson, Minnesota Vikings

T.J. Hockenson's arrow is pointing up, for a couple of reasons. Having Cousins back behind center certainly helps, and Hockenson has emerged as Cousins' No. 2 target with Jordan Addison sidelined.

Hockenson has reached double-digit fantasy points in three of his last four games, and he even came through against San Francisco. The Falcons have surrendered just under 10 fantasy points per game to opposing tight ends in 2026.

Chigoziem Okonkwo, Washington Commanders

While Mark Andrews appeared to be back on a good fantasy track two weeks ago, he was far more disappointing in his second game with quarterback Jacoby Brissett. The veteran pass-catcher was only targeted three times and finished with 3.4 fantasy points.

Managers can't trust Andrews to bounce back this week against the Houston Texans. While Houston has been vulnerable to opposing wide receivers, it has surrendered the fewest fantasy points to opposing tight ends.

articles.title: Steelers' Art Rooney II Addresses Aaron Rodgers & McCarthy, 'Insubordination Will Not Be Tolerated'
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers owner Art Rooney II has addressed the recent comments from Aaron Rodgers about head coach Mike McCarthy and the follow-up decision to release the veteran quarterback.
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Steelers owner Art Rooney II has addressed the recent comments from Aaron Rodgers about head coach Mike McCarthy and the follow-up decision to release the veteran quarterback.

Speaking to Gerry Dulac of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette , Rooney explained "insubordination will not be tolerated" while expressing full confidence in McCarthy to lead the team:

"I just want to say that I have 100% confidence in Mike McCarthy and I expect he'll be our coach this season, next season and beyond. The big thing, what happened this week, is insubordination can't be tolerated in any organization. When you start getting ultimatums, you can't live with that."

As far as the decision to release Rodgers, Rooney said a "change had to be made" and he agrees "with the change and the way it was handled."

In a statement to ESPN's Brooke Pryor , Rooney expressed he was "disappointed" with how things played out with Rodgers:

"I am disappointed in where this went with Aaron Rodgers, but I have 100% confidence in Mike McCarthy. And I have tremendous confidence in Mason Rudolph and the other players in our locker room. Decisions were made on what we believe is in the best interest of the Pittsburgh Steelers. Our main focus right now is preparing for tomorrow's game."

The situation with Rodgers began to dissolve late Tuesday night when the Steelers released a statement announcing he would be inactive for Friday's game against the Denver Broncos and Mason Rudolph would get the start.

Rodgers dramatically escalated things on Wednesday when he appeared on The Pat McAfee Show to rail against McCarthy for a number of things, including saying he fell asleep multiple times in a recent quarterbacks meeting, questioned his health, missed walkthroughs and team meetings and broke down the halftime huddle in Sunday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles by saying "1-2-3 Packers."

Rooney dismissed there is anything wrong with McCarthy's health.

"Mike's as healthy as the rest of us," Rooney told Dulac. "Health was not an issue. I'm not sure where that part comes."

Some of the details mentioned by Rodgers were confirmed by follow-up reporting. McCarthy himself acknowledged the "1-2-3 Packers" situation during a Wednesday press conference, calling it an "embarrassing" mistake.

Rooney told Dulac the comments from Rodgers was unfair to the Steelers players while they are preparing to play in a game this week.

"There's maybe a time and place after the season if he wanted to kind of unload," Rooney said. "He talks about wanting to be a good teammate, but you don't do that to your teammates a couple days before the game, that's for sure."

Despite the questions around McCarthy in the wake of Rodgers' comments, Rooney said the organization is "100 percent" committed to him as their head coach now and in the future.

McCarthy has led the Steelers to a 6-4 record through 10 games in his first season as head coach.

The Steelers haven't had a losing season since 2003 when they finished 6-10. They have made the playoffs in each of the past three seasons, but their last postseason victory came during the 2016 season when they reached the AFC Championship Game.

articles.title: Terrell Owens brings race into Aaron Rodgers conversation after QB torched Steelers coach before release
articles.summary: Terrell Owens claims a racial double standard in the NFL, saying he'd be called a cancer for Aaron Rodgers' behavior while Rodgers faces no backlash.

And everybody’s like, ‘Oh, why does it always have to be race?’ That’s a good damn question. Why does it? Why does it have to be about race? Why can’t everybody be treated equal?" articles.title: Colston Loveland Injured, Latest on Bears TE After Being Carted Off vs. Lions on Thanksgiving
articles.summary: Chicago Bears tight end Colston Loveland was ruled out of Thursday's Thanksgiving road game against the Detroit Lions due to a knee injury.
articles.body:
Chicago Bears tight end Colston Loveland was ruled out of Thursday's Thanksgiving road game against the Detroit Lions due to a knee injury.

NWI.com's Mason Williams posted a video of Loveland getting carted from the sidelines to the locker room with a towel draped over his head:

On the CBS broadcast, play-by-play announcer Jim Nantz said Loveland "got rolled up on" during Chicago's second drive of the game.

ESPN's Field Yates noted that Loveland appeared to be "visibly upset" when shown on the sidelines after getting injured.

On Chicago's first drive of the game, the offense was moving the ball deep into Detroit territory when Loveland made a five-yard reception.

However, Loveland had the ball punched out of his grasp by Lions pass-rusher Derrick Moore, and Detroit recovered the fumble:

Loveland seemed to get his legs twisted up while getting tackled on the play, which allowed Moore to come in and force the fumble.

It wasn't until the next drive that Loveland got injured and ruled out for the remainder of the game, though.

Selected 10th overall by the Bears in the 2025 NFL draft, Loveland was widely expected to take a big leap forward and establish himself as one of the NFL's top tight ends this season.

While he has had his ups and downs, he entered Thursday's game with 40 catches for 392 yards and three touchdowns on the season, ranking him second on the team in receptions and receiving touchdowns, and third in receiving yardage.

Loveland's injury looms even larger due to the fact that the Bears' other highly touted tight end, Cole Kmet, is already out for the season with a knee injury.

The next men up on Chicago's depth chart at tight end are rookie third-round pick Sam Roush and Stephen Carlson.

Roush entered Thursday with six receptions for 75 yards on the season, while Carlson had yet to make a catch and hadn't registered an NFL reception since 2020.

articles.summary: Caleb Williams drew criticism in September for pacing during the anthem at Soldier Field, but Thanksgiving's NFC North game showed a different side.
articles.body: Let's agree that a snapshot in time isn't a full picture of what's happening and Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams might have learned that in September when he was caught on camera during a "Monday Night Football" game pacing the sidelines during the national anthem. Casually moving here and there while the Soldier Field crowd and teammates on the Bears sideline stood for the Star Spangled banner earned Williams some online criticism – probably warranted. And during "The Star Spangled Banner" the network cameras focused on the Bears quarterback for a few seconds. Williams was standing in one spot, not pacing. And he was singing along with artist Antonio Cipriano's rendition of the national anthem. Let that marinate: Caleb Williams was singing the national anthem on the Bears sideline on Thanksgiving Day. Didn't have that one on the bingo card. Williams, as we all know, marches to the beat of his own drum both in how he plays and carries himself in his personal life. Unlike most other NFL quarterback, Williams throws with his index finger placed directly over the nose of the football. That is a rare mechanical quirk famously used by Hall of Famer Terry Bradshaw to generate extra velocity and spin. articles.title: Chargers Sign New QB to Contract with Justin Herbert Injured in Concussion Protocol
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Chargers are seemingly preparing for the possibility of being without starting quarterback Justin Herbert against the New England Patriots on Sunday.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Chargers are seemingly preparing for the possibility of being without starting quarterback Justin Herbert against the New England Patriots on Sunday.

The Chargers announced Thursday that they signed veteran quarterback Jake Browning from the practice squad to the active roster.

Herbert is currently in concussion protocol, and if he is not cleared in time to play against New England, the Chargers will likely turn to DJ Uiagalelei at quarterback with Browning as the backup.

Browning, 30, entered the NFL as an undrafted rookie out of the University of Washington in 2019, and he has bounced around between multiple organizations since then.

After a stint on the Minnesota Vikings' practice squad to start his career, Browning was with the Cincinnati Bengals from 2021 to 2025, and that is where he first saw regular-season game action.

In 2023, Browning went 4-3 in seven starts for the Bengals, completing a league-high 70.4 percent of his passes for 1,936 yards, 12 touchdowns and seven interceptions.

Browning also made three starts for Cincinnati last season, but he largely struggled, going 0-3, and completing 64.8 percent of his passing attempts for 771 yards, six touchdowns and eight picks.

After spending time with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the preseason, Browning was released, and he was signed to the Chargers' practice squad in October.

The Chargers are coming off a 27-24 loss to the New York Jets last week, which dropped them to 1-9 on the season.

Herbert, who accounted for three total touchdowns in the defeat, was placed in concussion protocol on Monday.

If Herbert cannot play on Sunday, it would put Uiagalelei in line for his first career NFL regular-season start.

Uiagalelei saw his first regular-season game action on Nov. 8 when he went 2-of-7 for 24 yards with one touchdown and no interceptions in a 44-22 loss to the Houston Texans.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers: Quarterback 'losing respect' as NFL reacts to stunning Mike McCarthy claims
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers claims that head coach Mike McCarthy was 'snoring' in a quarterback meeting in an explosive interview; Steelers president Art Rooney II comes out in "100 per cent" support of McCarthy after team releases Rodgers in light of comments
articles.body:
Rodgers sent shockwaves through the NFL on Thanksgiving Eve as he used an interview on The Pat McAfee Show to claim McCarthy had been "falling asleep in meetings" while suggesting his entire team believed a change was required on the sideline.

It came after Rodgers was benched for Friday's matchup with the Denver Broncos following two straight defeats, with Mason Rudolph due to start under center.

The Steelers later released Rodgers 11 weeks into what is set to be the final season of the 42-year-old's career.

"First of all, I don't want to be on Aaron Rodgers' bad side. Let's start there. We all make mistakes, right? We all do things that aren't necessarily right in the moment," said Sky Sports NFL's Bell .

"But when I look at him as a player, he wasn't playing well. He wasn't helping his team.

"And you could could see him and his head coach arguing on the sideline with with each other. They weren't getting along.

"Whatever happens behind closed doors, that goes down, but the response to it is where I'm losing a little respect.

"In that locker room is a sanctuary. Some things we just don't let out. We don't have those conversations in public - it's a respect thing.

"If Rodgers was playing MVP football like he did before, he could say all these things and get away with it, but you have to know where you are in your career."

Rodgers suggested in his appearance on The Pat McAfee Show that the prospect of being benched had never been mentioned during recent conversations with McCarthy.

He accused McCarthy of snoring during meetings and rebuffing Rodgers' suggestions that he needed to make more of an effort of connecting with the Steelers' defensive players.

Rodgers added that the "final straw" came during half-time of a game when McCarthy closed a team talk by shouting 'one, two, three, Packers!'.

Rodgers and McCarthy spent 13 seasons together with the Packers from 2006-2018, reaching the playoffs nine times and winning one Super Bowl. They were reunited this past offseason when the Steelers hired McCarthy following the departure of Mike Tomlin.

"I'm not sure what's next for Aaron Rodgers. I think he will figure out that for himself over the next handful of months, or whatever his particular process is," said Super Bowl champion and Sky Sports NFL expert Ndamukong Suh.

"But I want to go back to what Jason [Bell] said in the way that you handle your business, especially from the perspective of a star. There's a way you go about handling things.

"Those things should be handled behind closed doors before trying to get ahead of the story - on either side. Have a conversation, have an understanding, and then go from there and address it.

"Going out to the media and doing all of these different things, The Pat McAfee Show, it's great for them and great for ESPN , but it's not the proper way I would want to handle that particular scenario."

Responding to Rodgers' comments, McCarthy admitted to his "embarrassing" moment when mentioning the Packers during half-time of their defeat to the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 11.

Steelers president gives McCarthy his "100 per cent" backing

Steelers president Art Rooney II defended McCarthy on Thursday in an interview with the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette, insisting he supports him "100 per cent".

"I just want to say that I have 100 per cent confidence in Mike McCarthy and I expect he'll be our coach this season, next season and beyond," Mr Rooney II told the Post-Gazette.

"The big thing, what happened this week, is insubordination can't be tolerated in any organization. When you start getting ultimatums, you can't live with that. There's maybe a time and place after the season if he wanted to kind of unload.

"He talks about wanting to be a good teammate, but you don't do that to your teammates a couple days before the game, that's for sure."

Rooney II underlined his belief that events in the locker room should be kept within the locker room, and downplayed Rodgers' comments regarding concerns for McCarthy's health.

The Steelers are 6-4 as they prepare to face the Denver Broncos (8-2) on Black Friday.

articles.title: NFL Black Friday preview: Steelers cut Aaron Rodgers, turn to Mason Rudolph against hot Broncos
articles.summary: Pittsburgh brought the drama this week in the NFL. Rudolph has seen mop-up action in four games this season. He will make his first start since 2025 against...
articles.body:
Black Friday represents a new dawn for the Pittsburgh Steelers.

The Steelers shockingly benched Aaron Rodgers late Tuesday night, and then released him Wednesday. Pittsburgh faces the 8-2 Denver Broncos at Acrisure Stadium on Friday. It will be Mason Rudolph starting in Rodgers' place for the 6-4 Steelers, who are fighting for their playoff lives after losing two straight since their bye week.

The shock was less because of how Rodgers and the Steelers' offense had played lately — not well — but more so for how the Steelers and head coach Mike McCarthy had backed Rodgers and seemingly endorsed him, as recently as Monday. That all changed when the team benched him, prompting Rodgers to go on ESPN and rip McCarthy while declaring he wouldn't return to the team .

Rodgers reportedly issued McCarthy an ultimatum over total control of play-calling and the head coach declined, and sent the future Hall of Famer on his way in stunning fashion.

Amazingly, it appears as if DK Metcalf will play Friday, less than a week after being ejected from a loss to the Philadelphia Eagles … and it wasn't Metcalf's first such incident. He's amid one of his worst seasons to date and now must match up with Broncos All-Pro CB Pat Surtain II and do so with a backup QB.

Rudolph has seen mop-up action in four games this season. He will make his first start since 2025 against Denver, a team he's never faced. The Broncos have 31 sacks this season, and the Steelers have allowed 31 sacks.

Denver's defense has been closer to good than great this season, but its offense has picked it up after a slow start to the year. In the past four games, the Broncos have scored 26 or more points in each after hitting that mark only once in the first six outings.

The Broncos are riding a six-game win streak and chasing the top playoff seed in the AFC. The Steelers haven't lost at Acrisure this season, but they've failed to hit the 20-point mark in three of their past four games.

The Steelers are in desperation mode. They're currently in the seventh playoff slot and have a 57% chance to make the postseason, according to Next Gen Stats , as things stand right now. That might sound pretty good, and no team currently outside the playoff field is over 50%.

A loss would drop the Steelers' chances to 50%. A win would push them to 72%. Pittsburgh's next four games are against teams still fighting for the postseason.

It's not as if Denver has nothing to play for. It is currently the No. 2 seed in the playoff slotting, just one game behind the Bills, whom the Broncos host in Week 16 on Christmas. The difference between the top seed (which comes with a bye) and the next spot down feels massive.

But the Broncos are near-certainties to make the playoffs, currently sitting at 99% chances to get in. A loss would drop them all the way down to 98%. Their schedule prior to and after the Bills game is soft. It would be tough to lose to a team making a QB change in a short week, but it wouldn't damage Denver's playoff hopes much at all.

Since coming off injured reserve four games ago, Coleman has seen his share of the Broncos' backfield duty increase with each game. On Sunday against the Raiders, the rookie scored three TDs and ran for 111 yards for his best outing of his short NFL career.

The Broncos likely want to see what more Coleman can do, especially with J.K. Dobbins suspended for this game. Perhaps not coincidentally, during Coleman's strong four-game span, Bo Nix and Denver's passing game have produced four straight games with 200-plus passing yards.

The Steelers rank third in rushing yards allowed and fourth in yards per carry allowed. They've had a stout rush defense all season, especially recently allowing only 221 rushing yards in their past four outings. It could be a tougher assignment, however, if Alex Highsmith (ankle) can't go, as expected. Mike McCarthy said it will be "tough for [Highsmith] to make it this week."

Is there a less impressive team with a great record than the Denver Broncos? Tied for the best mark against the spread entering Week 12 (8-2 ATS), Denver has won six straight games — and could've fairly easily lost four of them. However, its schedule sets up remarkably well for a run at the AFC's No. 1 seed if the Broncos can keep winning as a favorite. Denver is a 3.5-point road favorite in this one at Pittsburgh, and it's hard to find a lot of reasons to be excited about the Steelers going with backup QB Mason Rudolph. And while Bo Nix's Total QBR is only 48.2, Denver's defense is a much better unit than Pittsburgh's. The Steelers' playoff chances continue to dim with a loss here. — Ben Fawkes

Scoring expectations are muted (36.5 total) as the Broncos and Steelers meet for a Black Friday afternoon game. Here are three fantasy themes to unpack as you watch the game.

1. Can Mason Rudolph get Pittsburgh's passing game going? Aaron Rodgers has not played well for several weeks, but it was still a shocker when his benching was announced Tuesday night. Rudolph has always been a capable backup through his seven-year career, but his overall stats profile to a less-than-average starter. Still, sometimes there's a bounce when a slumping offense gets a new man in charge.

2. Is Jonah Coleman too good to be true? Coleman was a one-man wrecking crew in Week 11 (three touchdowns, 129 total yards), and with J.K. Dobbins suspended for this week, Coleman's floor is especially high. Coleman is the current favorite for Offensive Rookie of the Year, a notable development given how little he played in the first half of the year.

3. Is Jaylen Warren still a Circle of Trust guy? Warren was seen as one of fantasy's right answers through the first two months, but he's in a 16-43-0 rushing funk over the last two weeks, with zero touchdowns. Rodgers' slump played into this, but Warren needs a decent start because Rico Dowdle is going to see work, too. — Scott Pianowski

articles.body:
Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert was placed in the NFL's concussion protocol after the Week 11 loss to the New York Jets. Herbert's status for Sunday's game against the New England Patriots remains in doubt after missing practice on Thursday.

Herbert went 15-of-21 for 131 yards, two touchdowns and zero interceptions. He added 32 yards and a score on eight carries.

Herbert has played all six of his NFL seasons with the Bolts, who selected the ex-Oregon star with the sixth overall pick in the 2020 NFL draft. His accolades includes the 2020 Associated Press Offensive Rookie of the Year award, a 2021 Pro Bowl nod and two ninth-place finishes in the NFL MVP race in 2022 and 2024.

The Chargers largely struggled over Herbert's first four years save for a lone playoff appearance in 2022, although that wasn't the fault of the quarterback. Jim Harbaugh then arrived in town in 2024, and this team was much-improved in 2024 and 2025, going 11-6 with playoff appearances each season.

articles.title: Steelers Activate Star WR After Aaron Rodgers' Release as Mason Rudolph Named QB1 vs. Broncos
articles.summary: Amid all of the chaos this week with Aaron Rodgers, the Pittsburgh Steelers are still preparing for a game on Friday and are getting help at wide receiver as Mason Rudolph gets ready to make his first start of the season.
articles.body:
Amid all of the chaos this week with Aaron Rodgers, the Pittsburgh Steelers are still preparing for a game on Friday and are getting help at wide receiver as Mason Rudolph gets ready to make his first start of the season.

The Steelers announced on Thursday that Michael Pittman Jr. has been activated off injured reserve after missing nearly two months due to a foot injury.

Rudolph was announced as Pittsburgh's starter for Friday's game against the Denver Broncos earlier in the week. He is line to be the starting quarterback for the remainder of the season after Rodgers was released on Thursday following his comments about head coach Mike McCarthy.

Max Hurleman, who caught six passes for 61 yards in his NFL debut on Sunday against the Philadelphia Eagles, is also returning to the active roster. He was reverted back to the practice squad on Monday, but a roster spot came open with Ben Skowronek going on injured reserve.

Pittman hasn't appeared in a game since Oct. 1 when he caught two passes for 15 yards in a 27-24 loss to the Cleveland Browns.

The 29-year-old has been dealing with plantar fasciitis for most of the season. He initially missed the Steelers' Week 2 game as a result of the injury before returning to play the next two games.

Pittsburgh placed Pittman on IR prior to Week 5 and he has missed the last six games. The Steelers opened his practice window on Nov. 18, giving them 21 days to activate him or he would miss the remainder of the season.

Things had been trending toward Pittman playing on Friday since he has been listed on the Steelers' official injury report as a full participant in every practice this week.

With Rudolph set to start for the first time since Week 12 last season, the Steelers need all the pass-catching help they can get to ease the burden on him.

Pittman will join DK Metcalf and Germie Bernard as the top three receivers against the Broncos defense.

The Steelers (6-4) are looking to snap their two-game losing streak that has dropped them to the No. 7 seed in the AFC playoff standings. They will host Denver at Acrisure Stadium on Black Friday at 3 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Blake Corum's Updated Fantasy Outlook After Career Night on His Birthday in Rams' Win vs. Packers
articles.summary: The Blake Corum takeover is complete.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams' running back had a massive night on Wednesday during his team's 26-13 win over the Green Bay Packers, rushing 32 times for 184 yards and a touchdown while adding two catches for 21 yards. His counterpart at running back, Kyren Williams, did have 16 total touches for 67 yards and a score, but he was clearly playing second fiddle in the backfield.

Corum now has more carries than Williams in three of the past five games and more rushing yards in four straight games. He's gone over 100 yards in back-to-back games and has a touchdown in seven straight games.

This is still going to be something of a backfield split, but it's clear the Rams are starting to ride Corum more as the leading rusher. And given the team's injuries to players like Puka Nacua and Davante Adams, grinding out games on the ground has become vitally important.

In other words, it's time to start thinking of Corum like an RB2 and Williams as more of a flex option, at least until the team gets healthier.

articles.title: NFL: Chicago Bears stun Detroit Lions on Thanksgiving with game-winning touchdown in final three seconds
articles.summary: Detroit Lions lead for 53 minutes and 31 seconds, stretching their advantage to 11 points midway through final quarter after Jahmyr Gibbs' third TD from 70 yards out; Rome Odunze scores twice, including game-winner, to clinch Chicago Bears comeback that secures top spot in NFC North
articles.body:
Rome Odunze's second TD - a sensational toe-tap grab in the back of the end zone - clinched the victory and deny Detroit, who had led by 11 earlier in the fourth quarter after Jahmyr Gibbs ran in his third score of the game from 70 yards out.

Chicago's lead secured right at the death was the first lead change in a game they've been involved with since they trailed the Carolina Panthers 7-0 in the first quarter of their opening game of the season. They had trailed the Lions for 53 minutes and 31 seconds of this match.

The Bears' dramatic win nudges them into solo first in the fiercely-fought NFC North, at 9-2 on the season, while the Lions drop to 8-3 with a first loss in seven.

It also improves Chicago's record in the division to 1-2, with Detroit now 2-1, which could prove crucial should any potential playoff tiebreakers be necessary to separate the two teams - who meet again on the penultimate week of the season - or the Minnesota Vikings (7-3) and Green Bay Packers (6-5).

The game was initially slow to ignite, with only a Lions field goal to show from the first quarter, before Gibbs' first score to start the second lit the blue touchpaper.

The Lions continued to lead thereafter, until the Bears came roaring back in the final quarter. Caleb Williams firstly located Odunze deep down the field for a 41-yard TD, the QB ran in the resulting two-point play to cut the score to three, before Jared Goff threw an interception on the next series.

Chicago turned the ball over on downs, failing to convert on 4th and 3 just inside Detroit territory, but they got the ball back with just over two minutes to go, and this time marched down the field before Williams linked up with Odunze again for the game winner with seconds remaining.

Williams finished with 345 yards passing and those two scoring strikes to Odunze, while Bears running back D'Andre Swift had 162 yards from scrimmage and a touchdown. Gibbs had 20 carries for a massive 205 yards and three TDs for the Lions but it didn't prove to be enough.

Passing: Caleb Williams, 30/44, 345 yards, 2 TDs

Rushing: D'Andre Swift, 9 carries, 65 yards, 1 TD

Receiving: D'Andre Swift, 7 catches, 97 yards

Passing: Jared Goff, 25/36, 313 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT

Rushing: Jahmyr Gibbs, 21 carries, 205 yards, 3 TDs

Receiving: Amon-Ra St. Brown, 7 catches, 146 yards

How the Bears roared back on Thanksgiving

After the Lions' first quarter field goal, they failed to add further points on the back of a Colston Loveland fumble, but they would find the end zone early in the second - Gibbs from down at the goal line - as the Bears offense was slow to fire.

Chicago finally sparked into life in the second and tied the game up at 10-10 with the first of two Kyle Monangai scores.

Detroit were back in front by the half, up 19-10, after a bizarre sequence saw them first awarded a safety as a Bears player deliberately batted a fumbled football out of the end zone, before Goff found Sam LaPorta for an 11-yard TD.

A second Gibbs touchdown was sandwiched in between scores for Monangai and Swift in the third quarter, while Jake Bates' second field goal put the Lions 29-24 up early in the fourth.

Gibbs only added to that advantage as he completed his hat-trick of TDs with the best of the bunch, breaking loose from 70 yards out but the game was far from over, with Willams and Odunze answering back almost immediately.

After Chicago failed to capitalise on Goff's interception, Detroit missed the chance to ice the game when opting against a 50-yard field goal try as they went for it on 4th and 4 from the Bears 33-yard-line.

Stopped short, Chicago got the ball back to pave the way for Williams and Odunze's dramatic, game-winning connection in the closing seconds.
