articles.title: Caleb Williams' Bears Spoil Gibbs' Hat Trick for Lions, Box Score Stats & Highlights for Top Players
articles.summary: Caleb Williams and the Chicago Bears completed an 11-point comeback to come out on top in an NFC North division rivalry, taking sole possession of first place in the division ahead of the Detroit Lions and Jahmyr Gibbs following a 39-35 victory on Thanksgiving at Ford Field in Detroit.
articles.body:
Caleb Williams and the Chicago Bears completed an 11-point comeback to come out on top in an NFC North division rivalry, taking sole possession of first place in the division ahead of the Detroit Lions and Jahmyr Gibbs following a 39-35 victory on Thanksgiving at Ford Field in Detroit.

The Bears overcame an MVP-caliber performance from Gibbs, who finished with three touchdowns and 205 total yards, by scoring a go-ahead touchdown with three seconds remaining to secure the win when Williams found wide receiver Rome Odunze in the back corner of the end zone.

Chicago entered the matchup as narrow 1.5-point favorites over Detroit, per FanDuel Sportsbook , and came away with a four-point victory.

The win solidified the Bears' hold on first place in the NFC North standings at 9-2, with a 1-2 record in the division and a 7-2 mark in conference play. The Lions fell to 8-3, dropping to 2-1 in the division and 5-2 in conference play.

1. CHI: 9-2 (OVR), 1-2 (DIV), 7-2 (CONF)

2. DET: 8-3 (OVR), 2-1 (DIV), 5-2 (CONF)

3. MIN: 7-3 (OVR), 3-1 (DIV), 5-2 (CONF)

The opening quarter was quiet for the Bears as Detroit opened with a field goal and its defense forced a fumble by Colston Loveland on Chicago's first drive. The Lions took a 3-0 lead into the second quarter.

The Bears found their first points of the game in the second quarter with a field goal before running back Kyle Monangai scored a touchdown to tie things up at 10-10.

However, the Lions remained hot in the second quarter, scoring a touchdown on a run by Jahmyr Gibbs before Williams was tackled in the end zone for a safety. Goff closed out the first half by finding tight end Sam LaPorta for an 11-yard touchdown pass with six seconds remaining to take a 19-10 lead.

It was a touchdown-filled third quarter as the Bears found the end zone twice. Monangai scored his second touchdown of the game before D'Andre Swift rushed for a 30-yard score to keep Chicago in the mix.

Gibbs also found the end zone for the second time with a 1-yard rushing touchdown of his own as the Lions took a 26-24 lead into the fourth quarter.

After a Lions field goal, Gibbs completed his hat trick with his third score, a 70-yard touchdown, to give Detroit a 35-24 lead in the fourth quarter.

It took just three plays for the Bears to answer, with Williams finding Odunze for a 41-yard touchdown pass before a successful two-point conversion cut the deficit to three, 35-32.

Dylan Thieneman came up with a tipped-ball interception to deliver the big stop the Bears were looking for, with a chance to take their first lead of the game or tie it. The interception marked Goff's first in a Thanksgiving Day game.

The Lions came up with a huge fourth-down stop, followed by a MVP-caliber run from Gibbs for 34-yards., but turned it over on downs.

Williams and the Bears converted on fourth down to keep the game alive, driving into the red zone before connecting with Odunze for the game-winning touchdown.

The Lions will hit the road to face the Atlanta Falcons on Dec. 6 at 1 p.m. ET, while the Bears will host the Jacksonville Jaguars at the same time.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers clears waivers, officially a free agent following Wednesday's release from Steelers
articles.summary: Rodgers, who turns 43 on Wednesday, is free to sign with any team.
articles.body:
Veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers passed through waivers on Thursday and was not claimed, according to multiple reports.

Rodgers was released by the Pittsburgh Steelers on Wednesday and was subject to waivers. After going unclaimed, the quarterback is now free to sign with any team, though it is unclear which teams may be interested given how he conducted himself this week.

News broke after 11 p.m. ET Tuesday night that Rodgers was not only being benched for the team's Black Friday game against the Denver Broncos, but would also be inactive.

Rodgers responded by joining "The Pat McAfee Show" on Wednesday afternoon and going scorched-earth on head coach Mike McCarthy for about 35 minutes. The quarterback went off on McCarthy, accusing him of sleeping in meetings, not watching film, and saying, "1-2-3 Packers!" when breaking down a halftime huddle with players.

While the writing was on the wall that Rodgers could be headed for a release, his interview with McAfee certainly sealed it. During his appearance, the quarterback even said he was not going to return to Pittsburgh.

The soon-to-be 43-year-old is now a free agent. Rodgers could land with a team that has quarterback injury problems or is right on the playoff bubble, but his conduct on Wednesday reportedly means that his options might be even more limited.

Rodgers may have played the final game of his illustrious career, but his tenure with the Steelers will almost assuredly be remembered for his rant on Wednesday.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers Clears Waivers, Top Landing Spots in NFL Free Agency After Steelers Release
articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers is officially a free agent.
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers is officially a free agent.

One day after being released by the Pittsburgh Steelers, Rodgers went unclaimed on waivers and is eligible to sign with any team.

If Rodgers were to find a team willing to take a chance on him for the remainder of the season, the likely criteria would be a club in playoff contention with injury concerns at the quarterback position.

As things stand going into Week 12, the New England Patriots have the most glaring need. The Baltimore Ravens could decide to try something drastic if they want to add another new quarterback after recently acquiring Jacoby Brissett.

The Atlanta Falcons could be a sleeper option since they are only two games behind the Carolina Panthers in the NFC South and Michael Penix Jr. struggling with six interceptions in his last three starts.

Any speculation about Rodgers getting signed comes with a huge caveat because a team would be creating a huge public relations situation for its players and coaches in the aftermath of his explosive comments about Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy that led to him being released.

Everyone on a new team would be asked about what Rodgers said and how it can go about ensuring no such situation will develop within their organization.

There's also just the general issue Rodgers has had at times in his career with not wanting to adapt his playing style to fit an offense. He reportedly gave McCarthy an "ultimatum" to "run things my way, or I quit."

In a scenario where Rodgers does get signed, the Patriots would seem like the frontrunner to do it. Drake Maye could miss the rest of the regular season after suffering a fractured right fibula in Week 10 against the Detroit Lions.

Tommy DeVito replaced Maye in that game, finishing 12-of-24 for 81 yards with one touchdown and one interception.

After Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Chargers, the Patriots' next three opponents are the Buffalo Bills, Minnesota Vikings and Kansas City Chiefs. They are currently 5-5, one game behind the Cleveland Browns for the final wild-card spot in the AFC.

Baltimore's season could more or less be decided on Sunday against the Houston Texans. A loss would drop the Ravens to 4-8 overall plus they would lose the head-to-head tiebreaker.

Rodgers would presumably welcome a chance to play for the Ravens, if for no other reason than they still have two head-to-head matchups with the Steelers in Weeks 15 and 18.

Quarterback really hasn't been the issue for the Ravens. Brissett has had some ups and downs in his first two starts, but he has thrown for 616 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions.

It's the Ravens defense allowing the seventh-most points per game that has been their primary concern.

The Falcons haven't shown any inclination toward benching Penix, but his recent turnover issues are the primary reason they have scored a total of 30 points in the last three games.

If there is one thing Rodgers remains good at, it is not giving the ball away. He has fewer interceptions (six) in 361 attempts this season than Penix does in 242 attempts (seven).

Rodgers isn't solving anyone's offensive issues at this point in his career. The Steelers wouldn't have originally benched him if he was playing anywhere close to his MVP level.

But history has shown desperation at the quarterback position will force teams to try anything if they think someone can help them win games.

articles.title: Latest on Caleb Williams Injury Scare as Bears QB Undergoes X-Ray After Clutch Win vs. Lions
articles.summary: Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams underwent X-rays for an undisclosed issue following Thursday's stunning 39-35 comeback victory over the Detroit Lions.
articles.body:
Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams underwent X-rays for an undisclosed issue following Thursday's stunning 39-35 comeback victory over the Detroit Lions.

The Chicago Tribune 's Brad Biggs reported the third-year signal-caller required some additional examination but that it could only be a precautionary move by the team.

After the game, Williams said he was fine:

The Bears trailed by 11 points midway through the fourth quarter before Williams connected with Rome Odunze on a pair of touchdown passes, the last coming with three seconds on the clock.

Williams finished with 345 passing yards and two touchdowns.

He told CBS Sports' Tracy Wolfson immediately after the game he tried to keep a level head with his team trailing late:

Williams undoubtedly earned his "Iceman" nickname on Thanksgiving, and he continues to thrive when the outcome is hanging in the balance.

With the win, the Bears improved to 9-2 and took a one-game lead on the Lions for first place in the NFC North. They could be headed for a second straight division title, something they haven't pulled off since 2005 and 2006.

Needless to say, an injury to Williams would have serious consequences for the team and put a major damper on an otherwise confidence-boosting result.

Having played mid-week, Williams and his teammates will have a little extra time to rest before they're back on the field Dec. 6 against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

articles.title: Dan Campbell Reacts to Lions' Collapse vs. Bears, Losing NFC North Lead in Thanksgiving Game
articles.summary: What a game.
articles.body:
The Detroit Lions lost a Thanksgiving battle against the Chicago Bears, 39-35, on a touchdown pass from Caleb Williams to Rome Odunze in the final seconds.

After the game, Detroit head coach Dan Campbell discussed the loss:

"They did what they had to do to win that game. It's frustrating for us, a number of things we didn't do well. Guys fought, those are hard when you lose those type of games. I just told the guys, 'Don't let this ruin your Thanksgiving. It's gonna sting, and it should sting for a while, but put it behind you and try to enjoy your family. It's Thanksgiving, you've got a couple of days off here.' And then we'll move forward. We'll clean it up Monday and then we've got to get ready for [the Atlanta Falcons]."

He also spoke on Jahmyr Gibbs ' massive day (205 rushing yards, three touchdowns).

The Lions looked in position to win this game after Gibbs rushed for a 70-yards touchdown halfway through the fourth, giving them a 35-24 lead.

But the Bears answered right back with a touchdown of their own, Jared Goff threw a pick and even after the defense stopped the Bears, the Lions again gave the ball back to Chicago after Gibbs couldn't escape T.J. Edwards on the 4th-and-4 pass with 2:22 remaining in the game rather than attempt a 50-yard field goal that would have given the Lions a seven-point lead:

Campbell, 50, has always been uber-aggressive, for better or worse. Convert that fourth down and the game would have been all but over. And there was obviously no guarantee that Jake Bates would have made the field goal (he was 2-for-2 on field goals and 3-for-4 on extra points).

Ultimately, Campbell is going to live or die with his ethos. Being aggressive earlier in the game worked out when he took a safety late in the first half rather than having field position at Chicago's goal line. It worked out nicely after the Lions scored a touchdown on their ensuing drive.

Campbell is who he is. And the Lions are still 8-3 on the season, in part because he doesn't waver from his philosophy and keeps pressure high on opponents.

articles.title: Cooper DeJean Injured, Latest on Eagles DB After Concussion vs. Cowboys on Thanksgiving
articles.summary: Thanksgiving didn't get off to a great start for the Philadelphia Eagles.
articles.body:
Thanksgiving didn't get off to a great start for the Philadelphia Eagles.

Star cornerback Cooper DeJean was officially ruled out for the remainder of Thursday's matchup against the Dallas Cowboys after suffering a concussion on the game's first possession.

Kenny Moore II is the backup option at slot corner.

DeJean, 23, primarily plays shot corner for the Eagles, though he's also been utilized out wide and even at safety in the team's base defense during his young career. He's registered 56 tackles (five for loss), one interception, six passes defensed and a quarterback hit this season.

The third-year corner won a Super Bowl with the Eagles in his rookie campaign and was both a Pro Bowler and first-team All-Pro selection last season. He's a core piece on the team's defense alongside shutdown corner Quinyon Mitchell, linebacker Zack Baun and defensive tackle Jalen Carter.

But injuries have ravaged the Eagles all season long. Baun was out for Thursday's contest, running back Saquon Barkley and tight end Dallas Goedert also left the game injury issues, quarterback Jalen Hurts is out for the season and players like DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks, among others, have all missed time this season.

It's a lost season in Philadelphia. Eagles fans are already rooting for draft position. DeJean's injury on Sunday was just piling on.

articles.title: Saquan Barkley injury update: Latest news on Eagles RB after he left game vs Cowboys
articles.summary: Eagles star RB Saquon Barkley was taken off the field in the 2nd quarter.
articles.body:
Philadelphia Eagles star RB Saquon Barkley left the NFL game against the Dallas Cowboys. He is the 3rd Eagles star to leave the game so far in the early going. Dallas Goedert and Cooper DeJean also left the game earlier. DeJean will not return, while Goedert is questionable to return.

Barkley exited Philadelphia's Week 11 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers in the fourth quarter after taking a hard hit on a five-yard run. He did not return, and the initial concern was an injury to his left arm.

The Eagles later listed Barkley with a neck injury and an illness. He was limited in Monday's estimated practice report before upgrading to full participation Tuesday and Wednesday.

Philadelphia's final injury report did not include Barkley, meaning he was cleared for the Week 12 game against Dallas.

Saquon Barkley (stinger) is questionable to return to Thursday's Week 12 game against the Dallas Cowboys

This is a concerning development for the Philadelphia Eagles, particularly because Barkley had dealt with a possible stinger earlier in the season.

Barkley's availability for the remainder of Thursday's matchup will depend on how he responds to the injury evaluation. If he cannot return, Philadelphia will need to rely more heavily on its other running backs.

A stinger can affect a player's shoulder, arm, and neck, making his ability to return uncertain. For now, the Eagles will lean on RB Will Shipley to hold down the backfield, and they will be relying on QB Joe Milton to lead the offense.

On the Eagles' first drive without Barkley, they did get into field goal range, and Barkley was seen on the sidelines itching to get back into the game. The score is now 14-3 for the Cowboys with about half the 2nd quarter remaining.

articles.title: NFL world reacts to stunning Bears Thanksgiving win vs. Lions
articles.summary: The Bears made this a Thanksgiving to remember following their comeback win over the Lions. Here is how social media reacted to the win.
articles.body:
Two years ago, the Chicago Bears had a chance to steal a win against the Detroit Lions on Thanksgiving. Quarterback Caleb Williams had the chance to connect with Rome Odunze on the final play, but the team bungled the opportunity in dramatic fashion that led to sweeping changes for the franchise. Two years later, that same duo connected for arguably the biggest victory in the Ben Johnson era.

The Bears stunned the Lions on Thanksgiving, winning 39-35 thanks to a last-second touchdown from Williams to Odunze in a game that didn't skimp out on the dramatics. Detroit got out to an early lead and didn't let up for the majority of the game. Chicago kept punching back to keep the score close, but the Lions, led by Jahmyr Gibbs, wouldn't relent.

After failing to convert on fourth down, the game seemed over at 35-32 late in the fourth quarter. But thanks to a Lions' failed fourth-down conversion, the Bears got new life, and Williams made sure not to waste it. He led the offense on the final scoring drive to give Chicago their first lead of the day and the win to improve to 9-2. It's their best start since the 2006 season.

Many people counted the Bears out of this one, but Williams didn't hear no bell. Here were some reactions on social media following the victory.

articles.title: Steelers' owner backs coach McCarthy after QB Rodgers' fiery exit
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers owner Art Rooney II on Thursday defended head coach Mike McCarthy in the wake of attacks by former quarterback Aaron Rodgers.
articles.body:
Nov. 26 (UPI) -- Pittsburgh Steelers owner Art Rooney II backed head coach Mike McCarthy on Thursday, a day after quarterback Aaron Rodgers was cut from the team in the wake of his fiery public statements about the longtime NFL coach.

In comments to the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette , Rooney called Rodgers' personal attacks on McCarthy during an interview on a national radio show "insubordination" that "will not be tolerated," vowing the Steelers are "100%" committed to McCarthy.

Rodgers, 42, was released from his one-year deal the team Wednesday after he told "The Pat McAfee Show" he could not return in the wake of McCarthy's late Tuesday decision to bench him in favor of Mason Rudolph for Friday's game against the Denver Broncos.

The four-time MVP alleged McCarthy had slept through team meetings in a remarkable personal attack during in the interview.

Rodgers' comments indicated "a change had to be made," Rooney said, "and I certainly agree with the change and the way it was handled."

The Steelers' president scolded the veteran play-caller for not being a "good teammate" by going public with his comments about McCarthy and throwing the organization into a turmoil before a key holiday weekend matchup against a top conference rival.

Asked about how Rodgers' tenure with Steelers has ended, Rooney said, "I'm disappointed the way it came out. We certainly had hopes that he would be successful here, and I thought at times we certainly got on a roll. We had high expectations.

"It's easy to say, knowing what I know today, what would I do? But we had a good experience last year, and so I kind of wasn't expecting it to go this way this year."

The unexpected finale to Rodgers' time with the Steelers came after the 22-year veteran had previously confirmed that this is his final season in the league.

The 10-time Pro Bowl selection and four-time first-team All-Pro is widely considered one of the best quarterbacks in football history but also was having one of his worst seasons, completing 60.2% of his throws for 2,241 yards, 16 scores and six interceptions for the Steelers.

He completed 68.2% of his throws for 227 yards and a score in a Week 11 loss to the Philadelphia Eagles.

articles.title: Raiders’ special teams can ill afford adding to the team’s overall woes
articles.summary: Two deflected punts against Denver Broncos is two too many as field position vital for Las Vegas defense and offense
articles.body:
Considering the team's defense ranks dead last in points allowed and yielding the second-worst amount of yards allowed, the Las Vegas Raiders special teams can ill affording adding to the overall woes.

Field position comes at a premium in the NFL and for the Silver & Black, a disadvantage of that nature puts Rob Leonard's defense in dire straits. Which makes the pair of times Raiders punter AJ Cole III's boots were blocked by the Denver Broncos in the Week 11 38-24 loss a cause for concern.

"I have to watch the tape," Las Vegas head coach Klint Kubiak said when asked about the punt protection in the postgame press conference.

"Two punts were huge. They were big," Denver head coach Sean Payton said after the game. "One of them I know was a rush. When you look at what that does field position-wise and just say it's a 40-yard swing, it's almost like a turnover."

Even a day later, when the NFL statisticians officially marked the two punts as deflected and not blocked — due to the ball crossing the line of scrimmage — a sour taste remains in the Raiders special teams room.

The first deflection occurred in the opening quarter when Denver's Sai'Vion Jones bull rushed up the middle and changed the trajectory of Cole's boot with his forearm. The ball eventually settled two yards past the line of scrimmage. The second occurred a quarter later with Dondrea Tillman tipping Cole's punt limiting the boot to just 27 yards.

It was indeed a forgettable Mile High outing for not only Cole, but special teams coordinator Joe DeCamillis.

Shoring up the blocking and protection assignments on punts is a must as the Raiders' Week 12 matchup with the Cleveland Browns was flexed to the Sunday night primetime slot instead of the standard afternoon affair it was originally was.

Everything gets amplified under the lights in front of a national audience and repeating the lack of protection which resulted in Cole's normally booming punts ricocheting off a defender's appendage isn't ideal.

With 40 punts on the season, Cole is ranked 12th amongst his punting brethren in the league. The 2,029 yards his kicking foot has amassed ranks ninth while his 50.7 yards per punt average is third-best in the NFL. Cole's 43.8 net yards per punt — average that subtracts return and touchback yards — is seventh-best as the league average on average yards per boot and net yards per punt are 47.7 and 42.2, respectively.

The 31-year-old punter has four touchbacks which puts him at fifth-most and with 15 of his boots landing inside or being downed in the opponent's 20-yard line puts him right in the middle at 16th overall. That's the area where Cole is under the league average of 39.9 percent of kicks pinning opponents deep with his being 37.5 percent.

In comparison, the Philadelphia Eagles' Braden Mann leads the league in punts (53) and yardage (2,566) and he also owns the longest boot of the season with an 86-yard blast. The New York Giants' Jordan Stout tops the yards per punt average at 51.7 — the Kansas City Chiefs' Matt Araiza is second at 51.0 — while the G-Men's boot specialist is atop the league with a 44.7 net yards average per boot. Mann also leads the NFL with 24 of his 53 punts pinning opponents within their own 20-yard line.

Place kicking-wise, Matt Gay has certainly rekindled the accurate and dependable ways with DeCamillis in Las Vegas, much like the duo had during their respective time with the Los Angeles Rams.

As noted in the tweet above, Gay's two best seasons in his eight seasons in the NFL were with DeCamillis in Los Angeles. The initial skepticism of Gay being a productive replacement for long time kicker Daniel Carlson have been certainly allayed.

At 22-of-24 on field goals this season, the 32-year-old kicker has the sixth-best accuracy percentage at 91.7 percent. Gay's long of 59 yards gives him the sixth-longest boot amongst his contemporaries and going 25-for-25 on extra points gives him the third-best percentage in that department.

Gay's misses this season were from 49 yards and 51 yards out — both in the month of October. The first occurred in Week 5 against the New England Patriots (Gay finish 1-for-2 on field goals that game) and the second a Week 7 miss against the Rams (he finished 3-for-4 that day).

With the 22 field goals and 25 extra points made so far during the Raiders' 2026 campaign, Gay (unsurprisingly) leads the team in points scored at 91.

For comparison's sake, there's only one kicker who hasn't missed a field goal attempt this season: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers' Chase McLaughlin who is 22-for-22. A total of 12 kickers are perfect on extra points heading into Week 12 action. The NFL average for field goal percentage is 84.7 percent while it's 95.5 percent on extra points.

Return game-wise, Las Vegas boasts one of the top kick returners in running back Dylan Laube.

The 27-year-old reserve tailback is one of two return men in the league to house a kickoff. The 95-yard burst Laube had against the New York Jets in the Raiders' Week 8 38-33 victory was the first end zone visit on a kick return this season. Baltimore Ravens wide receiver Devontez Walker housed a kickoff (86-yard gallop) in Week 11.

Laube currently ranks second in average yards per return at 29.9. He trails Buffalo Bills running back Ray Davis (30.1 average) in that department. In terms of total kick return yards, Laube is third at a tally of 956. Tennessee Titans wideout Chimere Dike and Cincinnati Bengals wide receiver Dohnte Meyers are ahead at 1,112 and 968 yards, respectively.

The Raiders punt return game hasn't been as explosive.

Rookie wide receiver Malik Benson has seven returns for 94 yards while veteran wideout Deven Thompkins has one for 18 yards and Laube has two for 13 yards. Las Vegas is more apt to signal fair catch than return punts.

articles.title: Saquon Barkley suffers stinger in Eagles' Thanksgiving game vs. Cowboys
articles.summary: Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley is questionable to return after suffering a stinger against the Dallas Cowboys on Thanksgiving
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles are dealing with another significant injury on Thanksgiving Day after running back Saquon Barkley exited Thursday's NFC East matchup against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium. The Eagles announced that Barkley suffered a stinger and was listed as questionable to return.

Barkley's injury is the latest concern for a Philadelphia team that has already dealt with injuries to cornerback Cooper DeJean (head) and tight end Dallas Goedert (shoulder) against the Cowboys.

Philadelphia entered Thursday's matchup looking to build on its Week 11 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers, which snapped a seven-game losing streak. Barkley's availability is particularly important for an Eagles offense operating with Joe Milton at quarterback and without Jalen Hurts for the remainder of the season.

The Eagles' ability to establish the running game and create manageable passing situations for Milton could become considerably more difficult without Barkley, especially against a Dallas defense featuring Rashan Gary, Donovan Ezeiruaku and James Houston up front.

Barkley also suffered a stinger during Philadelphia's Week 2 win over the Tennessee Titans.

articles.title: Sean Duggan Honors Brother Ryan In NFL My Cause My Cleats
articles.summary: Dolphins coordinator Sean Duggan honors his brother Ryan with special cleats for the Jets game. Read the full story on the NFL campaign.
articles.body:
Miami Dolphins defensive coordinator Sean Duggan is set to wear custom cleats this Sunday to honor his older brother, Ryan. During the team's matchup against the New York Jets, the gear supports the Down Syndrome Association of Greater Cincinnati. Duggan will join 40 players and eight coaches in the NFL's annual "My Cause, My Cleats" initiative, according to the Sun Sentinel . The campaign gives every participant a chance to highlight a personal cause that matters to them.

Ryan Duggan, who has Down Syndrome, lives in Cincinnati where their parents still reside. Sean describes his brother as a "baller" and notes that Ryan was a manager on his high school football team. The bond between the two remains strong, with Sean saying they usually talk once a week. Ryan works four days weekly at a local bank and simultaneously holds a board seat with the DSAGC. Baseball and basketball are also played by him in the Special Olympics. Sean recalls how Ryan often asks blunt questions about the team's defense after games, showing his deep interest in the sport.

The cleats are not just a uniform requirement but a tribute to a man who overcame significant challenges. Sean told the Sun Sentinel that he looks up to his brother for everything he has accomplished. "He's the most positive person," Sean said. "Everything he's been able to do in his life….he's seen a lot of adversity, and he's been able to go through it." This perspective shapes how Sean views his role as a leader on the defensive side of the ball.

Ryan's influence extends beyond family circles, as he is known in his community for his positive attitude. Sean shared a story about their time together, noting that when he visits home, Ryan suggests they "grab a beer." The pair shares a genuine connection that goes beyond the typical sibling relationship. Sean emphasized that Ryan's honesty and humor make him a special person in his life.

The Dolphins are using this platform to raise awareness for various issues across the league. Edge rusher Josh Uche will wear cleats representing Alabama Regional Medical Services to support affordable healthcare for underserved families. To honor his godmother Collette, Uche, a Miami native and Columbus High School alumnus, donning the gear. Cornerback Jason Marshall Jr. is also participating in the event. The league-wide effort allows athletes to use their visibility to support causes they care about deeply.

Rookie safety Michael Taaffe and edge rusher Rodney McGraw are both representing the National Alliance on Mental Illness. Taaffe is also supporting Texas Against Fentanyl in memory of two family friends. McGraw's participation stems from the tragic death of his former college teammate, Marshawn Kneeland, who died by suicide in late 2025. "Athletes, we are taught to be gritty, so we are the main ones that don't speak up, and I feel like everybody should just open up and talk to someone," McGraw said, according to the Miami Dolphins. Quarterback Kyle McCord is honoring his rescue dog, Junior, by supporting the Misfits & Underdogs animal rescue in Mississippi.

The Dolphins will take the field on Sunday, Nov. 29, at 1 p.m. ET for their game against the New York Jets. The contest will be played at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens. This follows a tough loss to the Buffalo Bills, who defeated Miami 26-9 last Sunday at Highmark Stadium.

articles.title: Eagles injury updates: Cooper DeJean ruled out, Saquon Barkley questionable to return
articles.summary: Injuries started stacking up early on Thanksgiving in the Eagles-Cowboys game.
articles.body:
Things did not start off well for the Eagles defense, with Cooper DeJean suffering a concussion in the first quarter against the Cowboys. DeJean appeared to lower his head when he went to make a tackle and ended up on the sideline in the medical tent before eventually heading into the locker room and being ruled out with a concussion.

The secondary already had depth issues before DeJean's injury, so it was Michael Carter who stepped up into his role at nickel.

It wasn't long after that, that the Eagles offense took the field, which resulted in Dallas Goedert leaving the game with a shoulder injury and then Saquon Barkley with a stinger. Both were listed as questionable to return, although Barkley did attempt to return later in the first quarter. Offensive lineman Tyler Steen was also briefly sidelined, but returned to the field shortly after.

Injuries have plagued the Eagles all season, so it's not entirely surprising that they would have several coming off a short week, but hopefully none of them are long term issues, and they can be a healthier team for the back-half of the season.

articles.title: Eagles vs. Cowboys, Thanksgiving live updates: Dallas blowout brewing
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Eagles are facing the Dallas Cowboys on Thanksgiving at AT&T Stadium in Week 12 NFL action. Follow along for live updates.
articles.body:
Happy Thanksgiving, Philadelphia Eagles fans.

Let's see if the Birds can score an upset win against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium in Week 12 NFL action.

The Eagles (3-7) are coming off their first win in two months, beating the Pittsburgh Steelers last Sunday — a victory that played a factor in the Aaron Rodgers-Mike McCarthy drama that has since unfolded.

More importantly for the Eagles, their 19-16 victory over the Steelers ended a brutal seven-game losing streak.

But now, the Cowboys (5-6) and their high-powered offense awaits Nick Sirianni's team on Turkey Day.

The Cowboys are in the hunt for first place in the NFC East, trailing the division-leading New York Giants (6-3-1).

Understandably, Dallas is a heavy 8.5-point favorite vs. Joe Milton and the Eagles, per FanDuel Sportsbook .

But can the former Cowboys QB spring an upset against his old team? Milton will need plenty of help from Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith and Philly's defense — which will have its hands full with Ceedee Lamb, George Pickens and Co.

The last time these two teams met was in Week 7, when Lamb had two touchdowns, Pickens scored, and the Cowboys won going away, 38-21, at Lincoln Financial Field.

We'll see if the Eagles can keep this one closer — or if it's more of the same on Thanksgiving in Texas.

Stay tuned for updates here throughout the game.

Saquon Barkley is questionable to return with a stinger. Dallas Goedert is questionable with a shoulder injury. Guys are dropping like flies. But at least Joe Milton is balling.

Milton had a couple of dimes on a drive that finished with a 48-yard field goal by Jake Elliott. Milton found DeVonta Smith, who went up for a 24-yard catch. And he escaped third-down pressure to hit Makai Lemon for a 20-yard gain.

The Eagles are going to need touchdowns, not field goals, in order to come back and win this one. But a positive drive.

This is getting ugly quick. The Cowboys took advantage of the fourth-down stop with a 31-yard touchdown by Kavontae Turpin. The speedster turned on the jets. Too easy.

The Eagles' defense should have been off the field before the Turpin score. But they allowed another long conversion, this time on third-and-16.

The Eagles' defense was going to have to play its "A" game in order for Nick Sirianni's team to be in this game. That's not happening so far.

That was some brutal stuff from Sean Mannion and the Eagles' offense. They had a nice drive going, marching 58 yards on 10 plays down to the Cowboys' 36-yard line. The Eagles went for it, which was smart. But the play-call wasn't.

The Eagles lined up under center with Saquon Barkley as the fullback and Will Shipley as the running back in a split formation. Instead of QB sneaking with Joe Milton, the Eagles handed it off to Barkley, and he was stuffed. Ugly stuff.

Welp, that couldn't have started any worse for the Eagles. The Cowboys went on an 11-play, 77-yard touchdown march on the game's opening series. Cooper DeJean went off with what appeared to be a concussion. Dak Prescott converted a third-and-18, finding a wide-open Ceedee Lamb. And Javonte Williams punched in a goal-to-go score.

Let's see if Joe Milton and the Eagles can answer.

articles.title: Russell Wilson Reacts to Aaron Rodgers Calling Out Steelers' Mike McCarthy in McAfee Video
articles.summary: Russell Wilson and his CBS Sports colleagues were critical of Aaron Rodgers after the Pittsburgh Steelers publicly threw his head coach under the bus.
articles.body:
Russell Wilson and his CBS Sports colleagues were critical of Aaron Rodgers after the Pittsburgh Steelers publicly threw his head coach under the bus.

Wilson (via Front Office Sports' Mark Maske ) questioned whether the narrative presented by Rodgers was all that exceptional. To him, it's not totally uncommon for players or coaches to "fall asleep in moments" given the mental strain of the season.

Wilson went on to say Rodgers is leaving the wrong kind of lasting image to a Hall of Fame career:

CBS Sports' Bill Cowher and Nate Burleson echoed a similar refrain:

Rodgers didn't take kindly to the Steelers' decision to deactivate him for their Week 12 matchup with the Denver Broncos. A day after the announcement, he went on The Pat McAfee Show and laid into McCarthy.

Among the allegations leveled by the star quarterback, he said McCarthy fell asleep during some meetings. The coach also capped off one halftime speech by saying "1-2-3 Packers."

McCarthy acknowledged making the team mixup, and an ESPN report cited sources who "corroborated Aaron Rodgers' account of Mike McCarthy."

But it didn't take long for an unflattering portrait of Rodgers' behavior behind the scenes to emerge.

On Netflix's pregame show Wednesday, Tom Pelissero reported "frustration had been building among coaches and some teammates about Rodgers." In addition, Rodgers requested to have more influence over the offensive game plan and challenged the team to "run things my way, or I quit."

Pittsburgh wasted little time releasing Rodgers after his broadside, and he cleared waivers Thursday afternoon.

There are multiple teams in need of quarterbacks with a little more than a month left in the season. The nature of Rodgers' exit from Pittsburgh might scare off prospective suitors, though. His appearance on McAfee's show could be his last meaningful act as an NFL player.
